<reason>An exceptionally close, high-quality debate. A built a strong, well-framed case (burden-of-proof inversion, irreversibility, "ask first or find out later") and answered both pressure questions directly and cleverly, especially "license the release decision itself" for open weights. But B's epistemic-capacity core was pressed with greater discipline and never squarely neutralized: B answered A's symmetry move with the disclosure-vs-certificate distinction (false assurance degrading downstream vigilance), defused the pharma analogy, and—decisively—raised incumbent entrenchment and geofencing in its opening, flagged A's silence twice, and never got a real answer beyond A's one-line "leverage" gesture in the closing. B also answered both of A's pressure questions honestly (conceding "None" on Q1 but pivoting to the layer argument; citing GPAI duties binding developers in advance on Q2). A was clipped twice to B's once, a further small execution cost. B left more live routes to victory standing and engaged A's best points more squarely than the reverse.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 1 (Turn 4): "Legal powers without epistemic capacity are decorative" — fusing A's misrepresentation-liability move with A's conceded absence of measurement standards, showing faults "announce themselves" in aviation but not in capability evals, and flagging the entrenchment/geofencing/open-weight points that A still had not answered (and largely never did).</best_rebuttal>
